Important new evidence•JAMA Neurology•November 16, 2026

Plasma p-tau217 added to estimated absolute risk of cognitive impairment

Higher Lumipulse p-tau217 shifted modeled 5- and 10-year risks of incident MCI, illustrating a prognostic use distinct from pathology detection.

Key quantitative results: At age 75 using average Mayo cohort sex and APOE inputs, modeled 5-year MCI risk was 7% (95% CI, 5%–8%) at 0.072 pg/mL and 17% (13%–20%) at 0.324 pg/mL.

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217APOEPrognosis

Added November 23, 2026 · DOI:10.1001/jamaneurol.2026.4292

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Higher Lumipulse p-tau217 shifted modeled 5- and 10-year risks of incident MCI, illustrating a prognostic use distinct from pathology detection. Use the results to understand how baseline risk changes interpretation, not to institute asymptomatic screening.

Study design

Risk modeling in cognitively unimpaired adults aged 60–90 from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (n=1,644) and ADNI (n=534), incorporating age, sex and APOE ε4.

Key quantitative results

  • At age 75 using average Mayo cohort sex and APOE inputs, modeled 5-year MCI risk was 7% (95% CI, 5%–8%) at 0.072 pg/mL and 17% (13%–20%) at 0.324 pg/mL.
  • Corresponding 10-year estimates were 15% (12%–18%) and 35% (29%–41%).

What changed

At age 75 using average Mayo cohort sex and APOE inputs, modeled 5-year MCI risk was 7% (95% CI, 5%–8%) at 0.072 pg/mL and 17% (13%–20%) at 0.324 pg/mL.

Strength of evidence

Retrospective longitudinal prognostic modeling study. Key constraints: model estimates, not individual predictions.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Use the results to understand how baseline risk changes interpretation, not to institute asymptomatic screening.

Field medical relevance

Interpret alongside these constraints: Population, competing risks and assay affect calibration; Not a screening utility study.

Quanterix or platform relevance

Use the results to understand how baseline risk changes interpretation, not to institute asymptomatic screening.

Access or reimbursement relevance

These results do not by themselves establish routine availability or payer coverage.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports

No. Risk model validation is different from showing screening net benefit.
